programs.active: Once per SCENE you may scatter proactively as a QUICK action: while scattered, your MEMORY cannot be scanned, revealed or stolen, but your programs are offline. Recall it as a QUICK action.
programs.desc: It cannot save your datacom. It can make sure the wreck is empty and the vultures leave hungry.

programs.name: Witch Doctor
programs.passive: While this routine is active, gain a LARGE bonus to SOAK against HEALTH and MORALE damage - but any damage that gets past your SOAK is dealt to both HEALTH and MORALE. The doctor stitches you together with thread pulled from both sides.
programs.active: The mirrored half of the damage can be sent to a willing connected node owner instead of you - the doll takes the pinch.
programs.desc: Half medical suite, half seance. The reviews are excellent and slightly frightened.

programs.name: Pinkeye
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, flood the target's HUD and optical feeds with corrosive imagery: deal POWER MEDIUM, 3D+2 TECH MORALE damage. On a CRITICAL SUCCESS the damage gains the ONG property.
programs.active: Same as base, and the target also suffers a SMALL penalty to AWARENESS and any ranged attack rolls until next maintenance - it is hard to aim through a screaming feed.
programs.desc: Neural warfare protocol that turns the target's own eyes against them.

programs.name: Killer nanobots
programs.passive: While this routine is active, targets under a LOCK-ON applied by your network count as VULNERABLE 1 against attacks made by your network (all damage types).
programs.active: VULNERABLE 2 instead. The target's own maintenance nanites are actively sabotaging it.
programs.desc: Turns the target's own repair swarm into a fifth columnist.

programs.name: Beryl Protocol
programs.passive: While this routine is active, during Phase 1 you may reroll failed AILMENT saves, up to the amount of CPU you left unspent at the end of the previous round (maximum 2 rerolls).
programs.active: The rerolls may be distributed to any connected nodes (maximum 1 per node, your unspent CPU still sets the total).
programs.desc: Monitors the wetware and burns idle cycles scrubbing whatever is eating it.

programs.name: Matter processor
programs.passive: While this routine is active, reload actions of connected devices improve by one action category, to a maximum of Quick / 1 round.
programs.active: In addition, once per round one connected node may reload as a FREE action.
programs.desc: Optimizes feed mechanisms and munition consumption across the whole crew.

programs.name: BOOMSTICK!
programs.passive: While this routine is active, TEK weapons you operate use the LOC power profile: POWER HIGH at short range, MEDIUM at medium range, LOW at long range.
programs.active: The profile becomes HIGH at short and medium range, MEDIUM at long range.
programs.desc: Retunes your datacom's output wavelength from conversation to demolition.

programs.name: Recursive Loop
programs.passive: While this routine is active, TEK weapons you operate gain the BURST fire option.
programs.active: In addition, once per round one of your BURST attacks may reroll its damage dice and keep the better result.
programs.desc: The same shot, fired again before the first one has finished being an idea.

programs.name: Ghost 2.2
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your SCAN and LOCK-ON actions do not reduce your obfuscation count - only offensive actions spend your cover.
programs.active: In addition, while obfuscated your HACKING, CYBERINTEL and OPERATOR checks gain +1 critical range (critical success on 9 or 10).
programs.desc: The look-but-don't-touch stealth suite. Watching was never the crime.

programs.name: Cyberwall Nano
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your node gains a LARGE bonus to SOAK against SYSTEM damage.
programs.active: The LARGE bonus to SOAK against SYSTEM damage extends to every connected node on the network.
programs.desc: The Cyberwall line's flagship: one wall, everyone behind it.

programs.name: Carnifex Ultra-Violet
programs.passive: While this routine is active, once per round one SOAK roll made against a HACKING, CYBERINTEL or OPERATOR attack of yours is UNLUCKY.
programs.active: Every SOAK roll made against your HACKING, CYBERINTEL and OPERATOR attacks is UNLUCKY.
programs.desc: It's a Carnifex. It devours defenses about as fast as your budget.

programs.name: Distributed Denial of Service
programs.passive: While this routine is active, TEK weapons you operate gain the FULL-AUTO option (on a hit, roll again at a cumulative -1 success until you miss).
programs.active: The first cumulative -1 penalty of each FULL-AUTO chain is ignored.
programs.desc: Why settle for one result when you can have all of them at once? Satisfaction guaranteed.

programs.name: Killdog Rexxx
programs.passive: While this routine is active, anyone who deals SYSTEM damage to a node on your network is automatically hit with one LOCK-ON ailment, no roll required.
programs.active: Attacks made by your network against targets carrying a Killdog LOCK-ON are LUCKY and gain +2 flat damage.
programs.desc: The black-market Rexxx. The stock model watches. This one bites back.

programs.name: Nordcorp Protocol 0
programs.passive: While this routine is active, every defense value of your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as a minimum of MEDIUM.
programs.active: In addition, your datacom's SOAK rolls always count as maximum results.
programs.desc: Trust me, this thing does not exist. If it did, hackers would be out of business.

programs.name: Basic Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least: Physical LOW / Energy MEDIUM / Tech MEDIUM / Spiritual LOW.
programs.active: Raise one rating of your choice by one category (maximum HIGH). You may change which rating each maintenance.
programs.desc: Better than nothing.

programs.name: Adaptive Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least LOW in all types, and as HIGH against attacks from any target carrying a LOCK-ON applied by your network.
programs.active: The rating against LOCK-ON'd attackers becomes EXTREME.
programs.desc: Broad low protection that hardens the instant the wall knows who is hitting it.

programs.name: Virtual Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least: Physical LOW / Energy LOW / Tech EXTREME / Spiritual LOW.
programs.active: In addition, gain a SMALL bonus to SOAK against TECH damage.
programs.desc: A specialist's answer to digital intrusion: one perfect wall, three token fences.

programs.name: Stone Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least: Physical EXTREME / Energy LOW / Tech LOW / Spiritual LOW.
programs.active: In addition, gain a SMALL bonus to SOAK against PHYSICAL damage.
programs.desc: For when the intrusion arrives as a swarm of very small, very sharp machines.

programs.name: Fire Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least: Physical LOW / Energy EXTREME / Tech LOW / Spiritual LOW.
programs.active: In addition, gain a SMALL bonus to SOAK against ENERGY damage.
programs.desc: The name is four thousand years old and nobody at the manufacturer knows why.

programs.name: Spirit Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least: Physical LOW / Energy LOW / Tech LOW / Spiritual EXTREME.
programs.active: In addition, gain a SMALL bonus to SOAK against SPIRITUAL damage.
programs.desc: Consecrated code. The license agreement includes a blessing.

programs.name: Combat Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least MEDIUM in all types. As a FREE action you may spend 1 NANITE to raise one rating by one category against a single incoming attack; it reverts after the attack resolves.
programs.active: The nanite spend raises the rating by two categories instead (maximum EXTREME).
programs.desc: Military-grade wall for combat engineers who expect to be shot at in four different ways.

programs.name: Slick's Wall of Awesome
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least MEDIUM in all types, and the first time each round you fully soak an incoming attack you regain 1 NANITE (up to your maximum).
programs.active: The matrix is treated as at least HIGH in all types, and the nanite regain triggers on every attack you defend against.
programs.desc: Flashy, loud, and it pays you to get shot at. Slick swears there are only three copies.

programs.name: Fly trap Wall
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your datacom's Defense Matrix is treated as at least LOW in all types, and the first attacker each round who targets your node with a hacking action is automatically hit with one LOCK-ON ailment, no roll required.
programs.active: In addition, steal 1 banked control token from each attacker the trap catches.
programs.desc: A baited wall. It is not there to stop you, it is there to remember you.

programs.name: Nulify Defenses
programs.passive: While this routine is active, once per round one of your hacking attacks may change its damage type to match the target's lowest DEFENSE rating. You must have learned that defense first (a successful SCAN or Deep Scan against the target this SCENE).
programs.active: All of your hacking attacks may retune this way, and you no longer need a prior scan - the routine reads the defenses in real time.
programs.desc: Tronik warfare code. It does not break your wall, it simply asks which one you forgot to build.

programs.name: Conference Call
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your ASSISTANCE basic action grants its SMALL bonus to every connected node instead of a single ally (each must still use it before the start of your next turn).
programs.active: The network-wide ASSISTANCE grants a LARGE bonus instead.
programs.desc: A corporate tool for assisting every employee at once, repurposed for people corporations shoot at.

programs.name: Cyber Mole
programs.passive: While this routine is active and you are obfuscated, gain a SMALL bonus to HACKING and CYBERINTEL checks made against the network you are hiding from.
programs.active: The bonus becomes LARGE. The deeper they let you sit, the worse it gets for them.
programs.desc: A patience program. Moles do their best work from inside the garden.

programs.name: Magnetron
programs.passive: Roll CYBERINTEL to flood the local spectrum: until next maintenance, all HACKING, CYBERINTEL and OPERATOR checks made within your datacom's short range - friend or foe, but not yours - suffer a SMALL penalty (LARGE on 3+ successes). Indiscriminate: your own allies are jammed too.
programs.active: You may exempt every node on your network from the jamming.
programs.desc: A brick of noise. Subtle as a flare, twice as useful.

programs.name: Reinforcement
programs.passive: While this routine is active, every connected node gains a SMALL bonus to SOAK against TECH attacks made from beyond melee range. DIRECT CONNECTIONS bypass it entirely - distance is the whole trick.
programs.active: The bonus becomes LARGE.
programs.desc: Signal armor. Works beautifully right up until someone walks over and plugs in.

programs.name: Pufferfish
programs.passive: While this routine is active, the first successful SCAN, Deep Scan or program reveal against your network each SCENE returns false data of your choosing instead of the truth. The scanner is not told their result was fed to them.
programs.active: Every scan against your network returns false data while you hold control.
programs.desc: Looks bigger than it is. Also looks smaller than it is. Whichever you need.

programs.name: Obliterator Protocol
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's SPEED. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 3D+1 ENERGY HEALTH damage.
programs.active: The attack gains DP (target counts as BREACHED, but you take a SMALL penalty to damage).
programs.desc: Reconfigures your gun from shooting people to shooting whatever they are hiding behind their defenses.

programs.name: FireZap
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's SPEED. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 4D+2 ENERGY HEALTH damage as directed nerve-scorching energy.
programs.active: On a CRITICAL SUCCESS the target also suffers the EXPOSED critical ailment.
programs.desc: It does not burn the skin. It burns the wiring underneath it.

programs.name: StrikeNet
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 4D+2 ENERGY MORALE damage.
programs.active: The attack is fired at POWER EXTREME instead.
programs.desc: It does not punch through armor. It punches through the will to keep wearing it.

programs.name: Cortex Killer
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER EXTREME, 5D+3 TECH MORALE damage. A hit that causes a mental trauma also leaves the target DAZED until next maintenance.
programs.active: The attack roll is LUCKY.
programs.desc: Skips the armor, the skin and the skull, and argues directly with the brain. The brain loses.

programs.name: TriggerHappy
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon as a needler: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's SPEED. On a hit deal POWER LOW, 2D+1 PHYSICAL HEALTH damage with the BURST option.
programs.active: Fire as FULL-AUTO instead (on a hit, roll again at a cumulative -1 success until you miss).
programs.desc: Cheap, loud and enthusiastic. Quantity is its own kind of quality.

programs.name: Killjoy
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 3D+1 ENERGY MORALE damage from disorienting high-frequency gravity waves.
programs.active: On a CRITICAL SUCCESS the target is also knocked prone (KNOCKDOWN).
programs.desc: The waves are harmless, technically. So is a rollercoaster, technically.

programs.name: MurderMesh
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the SPEED of every target within 2m of the impact point. Each target hit takes POWER MEDIUM, 3D+2 ENERGY HEALTH damage from bursting liquid plasma.
programs.active: The plasma clings: the damage gains the ONG property (reapplied at maintenance if the original damage was not reduced to 0).
programs.desc: Turns one bullet into a weather system. A small, brief, extremely angry weather system.

programs.name: NeuroStun
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 3D+2 TECH MORALE damage. Non-lethal: a target reduced to 0 MORALE by this weapon falls unconscious instead of DYING.
programs.active: A hit also leaves the target groggy: SMALL penalty to all their rolls until next maintenance.
programs.desc: The polite way to end an argument. The target wakes up later, embarrassed but alive.

programs.name: DeathWhisper
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 4D+2 SPIRITUAL MORALE damage.
programs.active: Any damage left unsoaked also drains 1 CHI from the target (if they have any).
programs.desc: Whatever is riding in the barrel, the manufacturer insists it is a waveform. It insists back.

programs.name: Verminator
programs.passive: Fire your TEK weapon on this protocol: choose the attack's damage type (PHYSICAL, ENERGY, TECH or SPIRITUAL) before each shot, then make an OPERATOR roll vs the target's SPEED. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 3D+2 HEALTH damage of the chosen type.
programs.active: The target's DEFENSE rating against this attack is treated as one category lower (minimum LOW).
programs.desc: A black-project chameleon round. Whatever your armor is good at, it is politely something else.

programs.name: Slurm
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage and apply one VULNERABLE 1 ailment instance (all damage types). Instances stack up to your EXPERTISE and are each saved separately during Phase 1.
programs.active: Apply two VULNERABLE 1 instances per hit instead of one.
programs.desc: It does not break the wall. It loosens every brick for whoever swings next.

programs.name: Smoke Break
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage and one routine running on the target network (defender's choice) is suspended until next maintenance.
programs.active: You choose which routine is suspended, and it stays offline for as long as you hold control.
programs.desc: Everybody out. The wall will be back after its break. Probably.

programs.name: Cry Wolf
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage. If you are obfuscated this attack does not reduce your obfuscation count - but when your obfuscation ends, the target gains a free LOCK-ON on one other member of your network (unusable if you are the only member).
programs.active: The frame lands wherever you point it: choose who the LOCK-ON blames, including a member of the target's own network.
programs.desc: The wolf is real. The name it cries out is negotiable.

programs.name: Black Out
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage and drain 1 CHARGE from one forcefield connected to the target network (your choice); drain 1 more if you beat the hit threshold by 3+ successes.
programs.active: Drain 1 CHARGE from up to EXPERTISE forcefields connected to the network instead.
programs.desc: Somebody has to pay the light bill, and tonight it is them.

programs.name: Exile
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage; if this reduces the target to 0 SYSTEM, one random client node is booted from its network and cannot rejoin until next SCENE, losing all network benefits immediately.
programs.active: No kill required: on any hit, boot one client node of your choice from the network until next maintenance.
programs.desc: The cheapest way to make someone alone.

programs.name: Power Surge
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage; if this reduces the target to 0 SYSTEM, its power source detonates: POWER LOW, 3D+1 ENERGY HEALTH damage to everything within 2m of the device.
programs.active: The detonation is POWER MEDIUM, 4D+2 ENERGY HEALTH damage in a 3m radius instead.
programs.desc: Every battery is a bomb with patience. This program removes the patience.

programs.name: Nurse CHAINSAW
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. No damage: on a hit, one node owner of your choice on the target network makes all AILMENT saves at the next Phase 1 as UNLUCKY rolls.
programs.active: That owner cannot attempt AILMENT saves at the next Phase 1 at all - the nurse insists they are fine.
programs.desc: Hijacks the medical monitor and teaches it to fight threats that are not there, very thoroughly.

programs.name: Friend maker 3000
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, add one ally of your choice to the target network's friend-or-foe list until next maintenance: automated weapons on that network (drones, turrets, TEK) will not target them. A wielded device can override this for itself with a QUICK DC5 TECHNOLOGY action.
programs.active: Invert instead: one automated device on the network treats its own side as hostile until next maintenance (same override applies, per device).
programs.desc: The turret is not broken. It has simply made a new friend.

programs.name: Hi I'm BOB
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, your node also benefits from one routine currently running on the target network (defender's choice) until next maintenance - their host thinks you belong.
programs.active: You choose which routine, and the benefit extends to your entire network.
programs.desc: Walks in, waves, helps itself to the coffee. Nobody checks the badge.

programs.name: Randomizer
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 3D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage, then the LUCK die judges: on a CRITICAL SUCCESS double the damage roll; on a natural 1 your own node takes the rolled damage instead.
programs.active: You may reroll the LUCK die once and take the second result.
programs.desc: Half attack program, half slot machine. The house is whoever holds control.

programs.name: Birthday Surprise
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 2D+1 TECH SYSTEM damage; if this reduces the target to 0 SYSTEM, you may detonate one explosive device the target is carrying (normal effect, centered on them).
programs.active: No kill required: any hit that causes a trauma also lets you detonate one explosive the target carries.
programs.desc: Everyone brings their own present. This program just unwraps it early.

programs.name: Nightmares
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the host node's WITS. On a hit deal only 1 SYSTEM damage; instead the host's owner takes POWER MEDIUM, 4D+2 TECH MORALE damage as the program whispers through their own feed.
programs.active: The MORALE damage hits every node owner on the target network.
programs.desc: It does not attack the machine. It uses the machine to attack the person holding it.

programs.name: Rabid Racoon 42
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 4D+2 TECH SYSTEM damage with the ONG property.
programs.active: While the ONG persists, the target's Phase 1 SYSTEM and MORALE recovery is halved - the racoon eats the repairs as fast as they arrive.
programs.desc: Black-market Tronik code. Nobody knows what the 42 stands for. The first 41 racoons do not exist.

programs.name: Code Injection
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit the target suffers a SMALL penalty to all skill rolls until next maintenance, and your node also benefits from one of their active routines (defender's choice) for the same duration.
programs.active: You choose the routine, and the penalty becomes LARGE.
programs.desc: A deep DISRUPT that leaves with more than it came with.

programs.name: Spam
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit apply the SPAMMED ailment: a SMALL penalty to all the target's skill rolls that persists until saved during Phase 1 (unlike a plain DISRUPT, it does not simply expire).
programs.active: Each Phase 1 the ailment survives its save, the target must also discard 1 banked control token - the pop-ups are mining something.
programs.desc: Congratulations! You have been selected. And selected. And selected.

programs.name: Nerf This!
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit the target's EXPERTISE is reduced by your successes above the hit threshold (minimum 0) until next maintenance.
programs.active: The same reduction applies to every node owner on the target network.
programs.desc: Precision is a luxury feature, and this program is the repo man.

programs.name: Decalibrate
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit the target's CRITICAL FAILURE range widens by 1 (a natural 1 or 2 on the LUCK die) until next maintenance.
programs.active: The range widens by 2 instead (natural 1 to 3), and you feel every one of them coming.
programs.desc: Does not make anything fail. Just makes failure so much more available.

programs.name: Gag order
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the host node's WITS. On a hit, until next maintenance the network's sharing is suspended: nodes cannot access shared MEMORY and hosted routines no longer reach client nodes - every member keeps only their own local software.
programs.active: In addition, client nodes stop benefiting from the host's defenses and control status, and the network cannot use the ASSISTANCE basic action.
programs.desc: Everyone is still talking. Nobody is being heard.

programs.name: Master Key
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your LOCK-ON basic actions are rolled as BURST (roll twice, keep the better result).
programs.active: A successful LOCK-ON against any node also applies one LOCK-ON instance to every other node and device on that network.
programs.desc: Why pick one lock when the building shares a keyhole.

programs.name: Publix Edumacation
programs.passive: While this routine is active, your SCAN actions also reveal routines: each success above the hit threshold reveals 1 routine running on the target network (still capped by your EXPERTISE).
programs.active: Routines you have revealed cost the target 1 additional reserved CPU each until next maintenance - you have seen how the sausage is made and told everyone.
programs.desc: Aggressively public education. The network learns what it runs; so do you; so does its CPU bill.

programs.name: Data dump
programs.passive: Run a SCAN as a COMPLEX action: on a hit add your datacom's EXPERTISE to the MEMORY stolen.
programs.active: In addition, gain 1 banked control token per 3 MEMORY stolen this way (maximum 2 per use) - stolen data is leverage.
programs.desc: Not elegant. A bucket is not elegant either, and yet.

programs.name: Thermites
programs.passive: Make a CYBERINTEL roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit apply one VULNERABLE 1 ailment instance against SYSTEM damage, plus one more instance per 2 successes above the hit threshold. Instances stack and are each saved separately during Phase 1.
programs.active: The instances apply against ALL damage types, not just SYSTEM.
programs.desc: A scan that leaves something behind: a map of the weak points, painted in accelerant.

programs.name: Proxymus
programs.passive: Make a CYBERINTEL roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, the next HACKING, CYBERINTEL or OPERATOR action the target takes before your next turn is intercepted: you learn what it is before it resolves and it suffers a LARGE penalty.
programs.active: Once before your next turn you may fully redirect one intercepted action to a new target of your choice - including back at the sender's own allies.
programs.desc: Every packet goes somewhere. Proxymus decides where.

programs.name: Extinction
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, deal POWER HIGH, 4D+3 TECH SYSTEM damage to the target's datacom. Any SYSTEM damage left unsoaked by this attack also strips an equal amount of MORALE from the datacom's owner.
programs.active: Same as the normal effect, but the unsoaked SYSTEM damage strips that MORALE from every user on the network, not just the owner.
programs.desc: Extinction does not crash a system - it teaches the mind wired into it to despair. A Tronik black-program of disputed origin, it pours corrosive feedback down the link until the hardware fails and the operator feels every byte of it die. Veterans claim you can tell a machine that was merely hacked from one that met Extinction: the second kind goes quiet, and so does whoever was wearing it.

programs.name: Marked Cards
programs.passive: Make a CYBERINTEL roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit, during the next Phase 2 the target must reveal their bid to you before you commit yours - for that one rivalry, the blind bid is not blind.
programs.active: Same as base. In addition you learn their banked control token total and any CPU they commit to the bid.
programs.desc: The bid is sacred and simultaneous. Was.

programs.name: Undertow
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER HIGH, 4D+2 TECH SYSTEM damage with the ONG property (reapplied at maintenance if the original damage was not reduced to 0).
programs.active: Same as base. In addition, each time the ONG damage reapplies at maintenance it gains a cumulative +2 flat damage until cleared.
programs.desc: Not a wave. A current. You notice when you are already under.

programs.name: Honeypot
programs.passive: Arm a decoy file (one charge per SCENE). The first time a rival's information action (SCAN, program reveal, MEMORY steal) targets you, it hits the decoy instead: the action yields nothing and the intruder is identified - they lose all obfuscation against your network and cannot obfuscate against it again this SCENE.
programs.active: Same as base, and the decoy tags the intruder: apply one LOCK-ON ailment to them, no roll required.
programs.desc: Free data. Help yourself.

programs.name: Vesper
programs.passive: Requires a consecrated or relic datacom, or the expenditure of 1 NANITE per use (the swarm etches transient runes into the signal path). Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS. On a hit deal POWER MEDIUM, 3D+2 SPIRITUAL SYSTEM damage - most datacoms never budgeted for a SPIRITUAL defense.
programs.active: Same as base. In addition, if the hit causes a mental trauma, a spellcasting wielder's spirit is also SUPPRESSED until next maintenance.
programs.desc: Somewhere a monastery is very angry about what happened to their liturgy files.

programs.name: Press Gang
programs.passive: Make a HACKING roll vs the target's WITS against a client node. On a hit, sever it from its network until next maintenance - it loses the host's defenses, control status and hosted software. Each success above the hit threshold extends the severance by one additional maintenance.
programs.active: Instead of severing, conscript the node as a hostage client until next maintenance. Its owner keeps full use of their own device - programs, CPU, MEMORY, nanites and defense layers all remain theirs; you gain no access to them. What changes: the node loses its former network's benefits, counts as a member of your network for any network-wide effects (yours or anyone else's), and cannot rejoin its old network while held. You must reserve 1 CPU to hold it, per normal hosting rules.
programs.desc: Welcome aboard. Attendance is not optional.

programs.name: Dead Man's Hand
programs.passive: While active, if your network's host node reaches 0 SYSTEM, connected client nodes do not fall with it - they disconnect safely instead, losing all network benefits but staying online.
programs.active: In addition, a pre-designated client node instantly inherits the network as the new host. Routines hosted on the fallen node stay offline until it recovers, but the network itself never goes dark.
programs.desc: Every ganger knows: kill the host, kill the crew. This is the crew disagreeing.

programs.name: War Chest
programs.passive: While active, your banked control-token cap at the end of Phase 2 becomes MEMORY + 2.
programs.active: Each maintenance you hold control, bank 1 bonus control token (no roll).
programs.desc: Patience, compounding interest, and one very good round.

programs.name: Quarantine
programs.passive: While active, designate one connected client node as sandboxed: attacks and programs that target your entire network do not affect it. While sandboxed it also loses shared-memory access - safety costs connection.
programs.active: The sandbox holds up to EXPERTISE nodes instead of one.
programs.desc: The medic's datacom does not get to die with everyone else's.

gadgets.name: Jury Rig
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and roll OPERATOR: the swarm physically rebuilds one machine or drone within datacom range, restoring SYSTEM equal to your successes. On 3+ successes also clear its COMPROMISED state.
gadgets.active: Same as base, and you may also clear CRIPPLED; successes beyond what the first machine needs spill onto a second machine in range.
gadgets.desc: Duct tape at the speed of thought.

gadgets.name: Caltrop Swarm
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and roll OPERATOR: nanites carpet a 3m zone within datacom range until the end of the SCENE. The zone is difficult terrain, and anyone crossing it must pass an ATHLETICS check at a DC equal to your successes (maximum 7) or fall prone.
gadgets.active: The swarm is mobile - shift the zone up to 5m each round as a free action.
gadgets.desc: The oldest weapon in history, now with firmware.

gadgets.name: Scaffold
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: nanites assemble one physical structure within datacom range - bridge, ramp, ladder or barricade. Maximum footprint 3m x 3m, maximum span or height 3m, supports up to 500 kg. It is a basic-tier device (one successful hit or hack destroys it) with STRUCTURE 5, blocks line of sight, and used as a barricade it grants standard COVER to anyone behind it. Lasts until the end of the SCENE.
gadgets.active: The structure is dynamic: reshape it once per round as a free action - raise the bridge, drop the wall mid-firefight.
gadgets.desc: Architecture, but in a hurry.

gadgets.name: Bloodhound Dust
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and roll CYBERINTEL: the swarm disperses as abrasive tracker motes through a 5m volume within datacom range. Until the end of the SCENE, Type I (visual) concealment of anyone inside the volume is reduced by your successes - the motes settle on whatever is moving through them and trace its outline.
gadgets.active: In addition, apply one LOCK-ON ailment to each target the dust reveals, no roll required.
gadgets.desc: You can fool a camera. Fooling ten billion specks of grit clinging to your shoulders is harder.

gadgets.name: High Powered Communications
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: the swarm forms a broadcast array. Until the end of the SCENE your datacom's maximum range extends to low planetary orbit. The array is a beacon: you cannot OBFUSCATE while it runs, and any action through it other than transferring information takes a LARGE penalty.
gadgets.active: The array whispers instead of shouting: obfuscation works normally and the action penalty drops to SMALL.
gadgets.desc: Turns your wrist unit into a radio tower. Subtlety sold separately.

gadgets.name: Anti-Theft System
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: for the next 10 hours the swarm guards your datacom or one object of your choice. Any tampering triggers an alarm audible at 50m, or a silent ping to you if configured that way.
gadgets.active: The swarm also tags the tamperer: apply one LOCK-ON ailment to them if they are within datacom range, no roll required.
gadgets.desc: Ten billion tiny witnesses with one job and no sense of humor about it.

gadgets.name: Scouting protocols
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: after a 5-minute sweep the swarm maps everything in a 100m radius - layout, exits, visible targets. The motes do not enter restricted or sealed areas, are plainly visible, and can be destroyed if seen.
gadgets.active: The motes linger as sentries: for the rest of the SCENE you are alerted the first time each round anything larger than a cat moves inside the mapped area.
gadgets.desc: The swarm fans out, looks at everything, and files a report.

gadgets.name: Do you Lift bro?
gadgets.passive: Spend 3 NANITES: for the SCENE the swarm either carries one item up to Ex.Large / 100 kg within datacom range, or braces your body - gain a LARGE bonus to ATHLETICS checks to lift, break, push, pull or hold anything up to 500 kg.
gadgets.active: Capacities double: 200 kg carried, up to 1000 kg assisted.
gadgets.desc: Yes. The swarm lifts. The swarm always lifts.

gadgets.name: Additional Storage
gadgets.passive: Reserve any number of NANITES: your MEMORY increases by the same amount. Reserved nanites do not recover between SCENES until released.
gadgets.active: The reserved nanites also raise your control-token bank cap by the same amount - more shelves, more war chest.
gadgets.desc: Storage made of the storage you were saving for something else.

gadgets.name: Hidden surprises
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: the swarm forms any basic (non-powered) MELEE weapon up to size Medium, using that weapon's normal stats, until the end of the SCENE. Wield it yourself with MELEE WEAPONS, or puppet it anywhere within datacom range as a drone with OPERATOR rolls.
gadgets.active: While puppeted, the weapon makes one OPERATOR attack per round without you spending an action.
gadgets.desc: You were searched. You were clean. The knife arrived afterward.

gadgets.name: Toolkit
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: until the end of the SCENE the swarm forms the tools required for one specific type of job. Basic but adequate - they negate tool-related penalties.
gadgets.active: The tools are masterwork: gain a SMALL bonus to checks made with them.
gadgets.desc: Any tool you can describe, one job at a time. Return policy: they evaporate.

gadgets.name: Smart Assist
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: one AMMO-based weapon within datacom range gains the SMART special capability until the end of the SCENE.
gadgets.active: The weapon also gains +1 EXPERTISE while the swarm rides its rounds.
gadgets.desc: Every bullet gets a co-pilot.

gadgets.name: Shield Link
gadgets.passive: Spend any number of NANITES: restore that many CHARGES to one forcefield within datacom range.
gadgets.active: Each nanite restores 2 CHARGES instead.
gadgets.desc: Emergency shield transfusion, one drop of swarm at a time.

gadgets.name: Adaptive Reinforcement
gadgets.passive: Spend 3 NANITES: the swarm forms a protective shell over one target within datacom range, granting one of HARDENED, INSULATED, HACKPROOF or SPIRITPROOF until the end of the SCENE.
gadgets.active: The shell grants two of the options instead of one.
gadgets.desc: Armor that reads the room.

gadgets.name: Infiltrate
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: after a 5-minute sweep the swarm maps everything in a 100m radius, including restricted and sealed areas. The motes are concealed (DC8 AWARENESS or SCAN to spot) and can be destroyed if found.
gadgets.active: The motes hold position on one device inside the mapped area: once this SCENE you may hack that device as if DIRECTLY CONNECTED.
gadgets.desc: The polite scout's rude sibling. No door is a door if you are dust.

gadgets.name: Parachute
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: the swarm arrests the fall of one person or object within datacom range (up to size HUGE, 200 kg), landing it safely.
gadgets.active: The descent is steerable: drift the falling target up to 10m laterally before touchdown.
gadgets.desc: Gravity still wins. It just agrees to gloat quietly.

gadgets.name: Meshed Systems
gadgets.passive: Spend any number of NANITES: restore that much SYSTEM, divided as you choose among devices on your network that are above 0 SYSTEM.
gadgets.active: Once per SCENE you may also revive one device at 0 SYSTEM back to 1 SYSTEM.
gadgets.desc: The swarm physically patches what the hack chewed through.

gadgets.name: Rogue Bane
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and set a trigger condition within datacom range. Until the end of the SCENE, if the condition is met the swarm detonates: POWER MEDIUM, 4D+2 ENERGY HEALTH damage to everything within 3m of the trigger point.
gadgets.active: You may also detonate it manually as a FREE action, and the blast is POWER HIGH.
gadgets.desc: A landmine with opinions about who counts as a rogue.

gadgets.name: Charging ports
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: instantly recharge one energy weapon, or keep one personal device powered for the SCENE, for any user on your network.
gadgets.active: Recharge or power up to EXPERTISE devices at once.
gadgets.desc: A wall socket that follows you around and never asks questions.

gadgets.name: Armor-UP
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: one target within datacom range has one DEFENSE rating of your choice raised to HIGH until next maintenance.
gadgets.active: Raised to EXTREME instead.
gadgets.desc: Instant plating, aimed like a compliment.

gadgets.name: Deep scanner
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: the swarm crawls over one object or target for a minute, mapping it to the micron. For the rest of the SCENE, gain a LARGE bonus to skill checks that rely on detailed knowledge of it.
gadgets.active: The sweep also reveals any hidden compartments, modifications or tampering automatically, no roll required.
gadgets.desc: Nothing has secrets at that resolution.

gadgets.name: Ghost Control Module
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: the swarm takes over housekeeping for one drone under your control. Until the end of the SCENE its basic actions cost you no CPU.
gadgets.active: The module manages two drones instead of one.
gadgets.desc: A tiny invisible crew chief for your drone.

gadgets.name: Nanocable
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: the swarm spins a near-invisible wire (1 HP, passive CONCEALMENT 5 vs Type I and II). Throw it at a technological device with a PROJECTILES check (range 1/3/5m): on a hit you are DIRECTLY CONNECTED to that device for as long as the wire holds.
gadgets.active: The wire is self-guiding: your PROJECTILES throw is LUCKY, and the cable pays out as you move, staying attached within 5m.
gadgets.desc: The shortest distance between you and their firmware.

gadgets.name: Workshop
gadgets.passive: Spend 3 NANITES: until the end of the SCENE the swarm forms advanced tooling for one specific type of job, equivalent to working in a proper workshop.
gadgets.active: FABRICATION checks made in the workshop gain a SMALL bonus and jobs take half the usual time.
gadgets.desc: A garage that fits in your pocket and assembles itself around the problem.

gadgets.name: Etheral Knives
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: the swarm condenses into 5 MONOMOLECULAR throwing knives or shuriken (normal throwing-weapon stats plus MONOMOLECULAR). Thrown with PROJECTILES checks; each dissolves after it lands.
gadgets.active: The knives reform in your hand at the start of your turn - the 5 are reusable until the SCENE ends.
gadgets.desc: Blades with no history, no serial number, and no murder weapon afterward.

gadgets.name: A.M.M.O
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES (4 for HEAVY ammo): the swarm forms a full S, M or L magazine for one AMMO-based weapon on your network. The formed rounds last until the magazine empties or the SCENE ends.
gadgets.active: The swarm-forged rounds are denser than factory print: +1 flat damage while the magazine lasts.
gadgets.desc: Never count your bullets again. The swarm counts for you, and the answer is always full.

gadgets.name: Shelter
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE: the swarm forms a rudimentary shelter around you. For the next hour you count as having INNOCULATION (protection against non-lethal environmental hazards) and gain a LARGE bonus to rolls against lethal environmental hazards and ailments.
gadgets.active: The shelter expands to cover up to 4 people and holds until you dismiss it.
gadgets.desc: Four walls and a roof, printed out of weather-hating dust.

gadgets.name: Kill switch
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and set a trigger of your choosing: when it fires, the swarm irrecoverably wipes chosen data from your datacom - or destroys the swarm itself - before anyone can read either.
gadgets.active: The wipe also plants a false trail: forensics on the device recover fabricated data of your choosing instead of nothing.
gadgets.desc: The best confession is an empty drive. The second best is somebody else's.

gadgets.name: The IGOR special
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: overload one allied DATACOM or DRONE on your network into a bomb. It detonates at the end of your turn: POWER HIGH, 6D+4 ENERGY HEALTH damage to everything within 5m. The device is destroyed.
gadgets.active: The radius grows to 10m and the swarm parts around friends: you choose who inside the blast is spared.
gadgets.desc: Every device has one last job in it. IGOR just asks nicely, then very loudly.

gadgets.name: Rip to Shreds
gadgets.passive: As a FREE action when your CYBER ATTACK deals SYSTEM damage to a target within datacom range, spend 1 NANITE: the swarm physically chews what the hack opened - the target also takes TECH HEALTH damage equal to half the SYSTEM damage dealt after mitigation (rounded up).
gadgets.active: Equal to the full SYSTEM damage dealt instead of half.
gadgets.desc: The hack finds the crack. The swarm widens it. In the flesh.

gadgets.name: Triage
gadgets.passive: Spend 1 NANITE and roll MEDICINE or LEADERSHIP: the swarm sutures, splints and soothes one ally within datacom range, restoring HEALTH (MEDICINE) or MORALE (LEADERSHIP) equal to your successes.
gadgets.active: The swarm also stabilizes: a DYING ally you treat this way is stabilized automatically, no DC.
gadgets.desc: A field medic weighing half a gram, everywhere at once.

gadgets.name: Opticloak
gadgets.passive: Spend 3 NANITES: the swarm bends light around you. Gain passive CONCEALMENT 6 when not moving and a LARGE bonus to STEALTH when moving. Ends if you take any damage, or when the SCENE ends.
gadgets.active: Taking damage no longer breaks the cloak - only the end of the SCENE does.
gadgets.desc: You are not invisible. Light has simply agreed to pretend.

gadgets.name: Tachyon communications
gadgets.passive: Spend 2 NANITES: until the end of the SCENE the swarm forms a tachyon array. Your communication range becomes inter-planetary, but the receiving device must also be tachyon-capable, and the extra range cannot be used for anything combat related.
gadgets.active: The array can also receive: you may query one distant tachyon-capable network for information as if you were a client node on it (with its owner's standing permissions).
gadgets.desc: Faster than light, slower than gossip.
